The libFuzzer entry and pcap-reading harness only deliver the pcap bytes into project parsers. This helper is the first project statement that turns attacker bytes into the internal entries-length state used on the vulnerable path.

For the witness, `lenEntries == 8` and the options-length field is `00 00 00 20`, so this check admits a layer that is 27 bytes shorter than its declared entries-plus-options extent. The patch fixes this exact obligation by checking the full entries-plus-options size and by validating option boundaries with `countOptions(count, data)` before accepting the layer.

Source step. `getLenEntries()` reads the attacker-controlled 32-bit entries-length field from the SOME/IP-SD payload and materializes `lenEntries == 8` on the exact witness. Those bytes are `00 00 00 08`, so later code believes there are only 8 entry bytes after the SOME/IP-SD header, which is shorter than one 16-byte `someipsdhdrentry`.

With SOME/IP-SD payload `dataLen == 41` and step 1's `lenEntries == 8`, this guard evaluates false because `41 >= 20 + 4 + 8 == 32`. The parser therefore accepts the buffer as long enough to contain the declared entries area and proceeds to read the following options-length field.

This dereference reads the attacker-controlled 32-bit options-length field at the end of the 8-byte entries area and materializes `lenOptions == 32` from bytes `00 00 00 20`. Because the whole SOME/IP-SD buffer is only 41 bytes, just 5 option bytes remain after this length field.

`getEntries()` reloads step 1's `lenEntries` as `remainingLen == 8` and initializes `offset == sizeof(someipsdhdr) + sizeof(uint32_t) == 24`. Even though `getNumEntries()` earlier prints `0` because `8 / sizeof(someipsdhdrentry) == 0`, the loop guard `remainingLen > 0` is still true, so parsing enters the entries loop on a region shorter than one 16-byte entry.

On the first loop iteration `offset == 24`, so line 499 constructs `SomeIpSdEntry(this, 24)`. Inside that constructor, `getTtl()` reads `majorVersion_ttl` at entry offset 8, i.e. layer bytes 32-35; those bytes are the in-bounds options-length field `00 00 00 20`, so this first constructor does not yet hit the ASan sink.
After the first constructor returns, `entry->getLength()` reports the fixed `sizeof(someipsdhdrentry) == 16`, even though only 8 entry bytes were actually declared for the entries region.
Subtracting `entryLen == 16` from `remainingLen == 8` underflows the unsigned `size_t` loop counter to `SIZE_MAX - 7`, so the loop state now falsely says many entry bytes remain.
The same fixed `entryLen == 16` advances `offset` from 24 to 40, moving the next constructor start 16 bytes deeper into the SOME/IP-SD layer, beyond the real 8-byte entries region.

Sink step. The second constructor's `majorVersion_ttl` field is at layer bytes 48-51 (`offset 40 + field offset 8`), which map to raw packet bytes 76-79. Since the allocated packet buffer is only 69 bytes long, this 4-byte read starts 7 bytes past the allocation, exactly matching the saved AddressSanitizer report.
